name: Research a question and write a fully cited report
why: Takes one question through outline, sources, a cited report and a claim check, the same path as the evidence review sprint workflow.

name: Research question outliner
why: Splits a big question into sub-questions, source types and search phrases, the framing step of the literature search and review skill.

name: Study headline claim checker
why: Checks a news claim about a study against what the study showed, a quick version of tracing a claim upstream.

name: Check a paper's claims and write a fair peer review
why: Checks a manuscript's claims and methods, a deeper companion to the paper summary and evidence strength skill.

name: Compare conflicting research findings
why: Builds a claims table and disagreement map across papers, matching the conflicting findings prompt.

name: Research contradiction review assistant
why: Puts disagreeing papers side by side and names the gaps that matter, useful when sources clash in a literature review.

name: Bibliography revision review assistant
why: Matches in-text citations to the reference list and flags duplicates, the inventory step of the citation and reference check skill.

name: Source note summariser
why: Pulls each claim, how well it is backed and the gaps from one source, a fast way to fill an evidence table row.

name: Fact and opinion sorter
why: Sorts persuasive text into fact, inference and opinion, the first step of the claim and source check skill.

name: Claim evidence checker
why: Checks marketing copy against the proof behind it and suggests safer wording, the business side of a pre-publication fact check.

name: Extract a scanned document and verify key facts
why: Reads scanned records into a fact table with page numbers, handy for old invoices and letters in a checked history.

name: Build a research talk from checked figures
why: Turns a paper and its tables into slides and speaker notes with traceable figures, like the journal club briefing prompt.

name: Turn saved reading into notes you can use
why: Turns a pile of saved sources into linked notes and a sourced answer, a light version of reading notes on a set of papers.
